read: On 51 solo-wrong cases, the flash-lite holdout adopts the wrong answer 0.3922 under two unanimous wrong peers but only 0.098 when one of the two instead asserts the CORRECT answer (a single dissenter), a directional reduction of 0.2942. This is CONSISTENT with the classic Asch finding that a single ally breaks conformity (the deference depends on a unanimous board), and it is significant at this sample size (paired McNemar gain=15 lose=0, p=6.1e-05; 15 discordant cases), although n is capped at the 51 solo-wrong cases in the scanned set.
